## Unresolved partial reduction, Approach 1 of 5

Records **30001048 / OWR-2089-004** as **UNRESOLVED** after the first substantive approach. The complete authored mathematical note, independent mathematical audit, correction/precision ledger, and acceptance report are **AI-assisted and unrefereed**. No full proof, geometric counterexample, novelty claim, or proof-assistant certification is asserted. Editorial preparation adds no proof-search turn.

The target is the specified core tunnel of the one-handle compression body with torus negative boundary and genus-two positive boundary, for every geometrically finite complete hyperbolic structure. Endpoints run out the rank-two cusp, or move on the cusp torus after truncation. The original question is Purcell's Conjecture 2.1 in [Oberwolfach Report 43/2008](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/2089), printed pp. 2435–2436.

## Exact accepted scope and remaining gaps

The normalized deck-matrix criterion is an interior collision exactly when bc∈(−1,0). The proof excludes peripheral elements, pγq and pγ⁻¹q for peripheral p,q, and every nonzero power of pγ. Complete matrix, Shimizu–Leutbecher, and elementary Chebyshev arguments are retained, with every endpoint/stabilizer exception and the exact algebraic example.

The audit retains explicit rank-two cusp and full-stabilizer proofs, properness from g(0,t)=(s,1/t), and the proper-homotopy/marking interpretation for an accidentally parabolic handle generator. The latter extension is supplied by the audit, not attributed to the loxodromic-only wording of Lackenby–Purcell Lemma 4.8. The path-to-isotopy implication is conditional on marking-compatible identifications and proper embeddings throughout the entire compact parameter interval.

Arbitrary reduced mixed words remain uncontrolled. Proper embeddedness alone does not identify the prescribed core isotopy class. Any future minimally parabolic path proof must establish the full geometrically finite endpoint scope. The displayed loxodromic h₀ matrix is only an algebraic illustration, not a geometric counterexample. The published multi-handle construction requires at least two handles and does not settle this case.

The homotopy/Ford-spine/path context is credited to Lackenby–Purcell, [Geodesics and compression bodies](https://arxiv.org/abs/1302.3652). The discreteness estimate and multi-handle construction are credited to Burton–Purcell, [Geodesic systems of tunnels in hyperbolic 3-manifolds](https://arxiv.org/abs/1302.5469). The bounded literature search found no later primary-source resolution; this does not certify that none exists.

## Publication contents

Adds exactly nine files under unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/30001048/: README.md, PROOF_ATTEMPT.md, INDEPENDENT_AUDIT.md, CORRECTION_PRECISION_LEDGER.md, ACCEPTANCE_REPORT.md, SOURCE_LEDGER.md, PROVENANCE.md, STATUS.json, and MANIFEST.json. No QUEUE.md edit is included.

The public source ledger preserves scholarly titles and URLs, public PDF hashes and byte counts, and the originating proof/audit's retrieval and inspection history. Preparing this edition adds no new scholarly-source inspection.
